Definition: of Hebrew origin (H2771); Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia:--Charran.
BiblicalUsage: Charran is the Greek spelling of Haran, the place in Mesopotamia where Abraham dwelt before God brought him into the land of promise. Stephen tells the council that the God of glory appeared to Abraham in Mesopotamia before he dwelt in Charran, and that from Charran, when his father was dead, God removed him into the land where they now dwelt.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Stephen names Charran because it is the halfway place again: Abraham stopped there, and God moved him on. The Greek spelling is only the doorway; the story is the same one Genesis tells.
